svg.title: Argument genealogy: dated versions of each argument, by topic and side
svg.text: Dec 2025 – Oct 2026 (by month; busier months wider)

g.title: 1957 · Haldane 1957: cost of selection, ~1 substitution per 300 generations
1962-06 · Kimura 1962: neutral fixation probability U = 1/2N
1968 · Kimura 1968: substitution rate implies many neutral mutations
1969-03 · Kimura & Ohta 1969: neutral fixation takes ~4Nₑ generations; fraction 1/2N fixes
1966-04 · Eden at Wistar: 20^250 ≈ 10^325 sequences vs ~10^52 protein molecules
1966-04 · Eden: hemoglobin α→β ~2.7 million generations, 'not implausible'
1966-04 · Ulam at Wistar: 10^6 successive improvements need ~10^13 generations
1966-04 · Mayr to Ulam: 'Couldn't they all go on simultaneously?' (earliest parallelism objection in the corpus)
1966-04 · Wright at Wistar: fewer than 1,250 'twenty questions' steps
1992 · Milton 1992 (via Day 2025): single protein by chance 1 in 10^65
2005 · CSAC 2005: 1.23% divergence; polymorphism 14–22% of it
2009 · Barrick et al. 2009 (LTEE): genomic evolution nearly constant
2012 · Balloux & Lehmann 2012: neutral substitution rate depends on N under overlap + fluctuation
2012 · Langergraber 2012: human–chimp split at least 7–8 My
2016 · Tenaillon 2016: non-mutators fit a model where neutral mutations accumulate at a constant rate
2017 · Good et al. 2017 (LTEE 60K): not periodic selection; clades coexist
2021 · Zeng et al. 2021: mean s ≈ 0.001 for negative selection
2025 · Yoo et al. 2025: 327 Mb SDR per ape lineage; split 5.5–6.3 My
2019-02-07 · MITTENS v1 (blog): 450,000 generations at 1,600 gens/fixation allow 562; 30M required
2019-02-07 · G_f = 1,600 generations per fixation (25 fixed in 40,000 LTEE generations)
2019-02-07 · Required fixations: 15M + 15M (2019)
2019-02-07 · CHLCA in MITTENS v1: 9,000,000 years at 20 y per generation
2019-02-11 · Gariépy (debate, via Day): bacterial fixation rate ≠ mammalian (sex, population-size variability)
2019-02-11 · Day's 2019 reply: bottleneck model cuts propagation time 1,600 → 15.7
2025-05-28 · Haldane table (blog): 300 gens per fixed mutation, 1,200 maximum
2025-12-24 · d introduced: ratio of actual to discrete-generation allele-frequency change
2025-12-24 · d ≈ 0.45 from LCT, SLC45A2, TYR
2025-12-28 · d = 0.45 ± 0.08 from LCT, SLC24A5, HERC2 (different locus list, same value)
2025-12-28 · MITTENS 2025: 146,250 effective generations / 1,600 = 91 fixations; 219,780× short
2025-12-28 · Required fixations: ~20M on the human lineage (from ~40M SNVs)
2024-04-25 · Spetner chain (posted by Day): 3.6 × 10^2738 to 1 against
2026-01-04 · Bernoulli Barrier paper: 14.7× available vs 1,570× required fitness differential
2026-01-04 · ~230 simultaneous sweeps; (300,000/440) × 230 ≈ 157,000 'appears to match'
2026-10-01 · Day: 3.0 omits the Bernoulli Barrier, which 'remains entirely correct'
2026-10-08 · Audit (F2, H2-hard): no saturation near 230 sweeps in the tested regime
2026-01-06 · Probability Zero 1st ed.: F_max = (t_div × d)/(g_len × G_f)
2026-01-24 · Samson (ally): total divided by time is an average whatever the overlap
2026-01-25 · Camestros: 'Generations per fixation' reads as one at a time
2026-01-25 · Camestros: Day treats all differences as post-split mutations (ancestral polymorphism)
2026-01-25 · Camestros: d is not defined (later corrected by the author: defined in Ch.13 / App. A)
2026-01-25 · Camestros: 'the arithmetic itself isn't wrong' (concession on the 1st-ed arithmetic)
2026-01-28 · Camestros: 35 fixed by 15,000 gens → ~429 gens/fixation (printed '1500', typo)
2026-01-29 · Camestros concedes: G_f was calculated as an average
2026-01-29 · Camestros: d would have changed over human history
2026-01-29 · Camestros: some lottery number is almost certainly drawn
2026-01-26 · McCarthy: 450 billion × 1/20,000 = 22.5M neutral fixations (N = Nₑ)
2026-01-26 · McCarthy: the Darwillion prices a pre-specified list, evolution needs any 20M
2026-01-26 · McCarthy: human genome ~690× E. coli; the rate depends on genome size and μ
2026-01-27 · Day: E. coli was cited for its fixation rate, not its mutation rate
2026-01-27 · Day: McCarthy's 40,000-generation figure raises the Darwillion 25×
2026-01-29 · keruru (ally, LLM-assisted): confirms the central thesis
2026-01-29 · N ≠ Nₑ: census exceeds diversity Nₑ 19–46× in mammals (start of the k = μN/Nₑ line)
2026-02-04 · Day (reply to McCarthy): k = 2Nμ × 1/(2Nₑ) = μ(N/Nₑ)
2026-02-04 · Day: McCarthy's model 'corrected' to N/Nₑ gives 8.25 fixations, 2,424,242× short
2026-02-04 · MITTENS formula stated on the blog: F_max = (t_div × d) / (g_len × G_f)
2026-02-04 · keruru (ally, 'mainly claude'): restates k = (N/Nₑ)μ
2026-02-07 · RRME: k = 0.743μ from four census cohorts, 'confirming' Balloux & Lehmann
2026-02-08 · Clock recalibration: CHLCA 6–7 Mya collapses to 200–580 kya
2026-01-14 · aDNA v1 (blog): zero fixations from <10% to >90% in 7,000 years
2026-02-08 · aDNA v2 (clock paper): clock predicts ~630, 21 observed; 99.8% before 7,000 BP
2026-02-08 · Day pre-empts ascertainment: the bias would favour detecting fixations
2026-02-09 · Six-country d–k regression: k ≈ 0.5μ or less
2026-02-14 · End of Deep Time: CHLCA 6.5 Mya → 68 kya
2026-03-04 · Bowers (reposted by Day): beneficial P_fix ≈ 2s, not 1/N
2026-03-04 · Day: the reviewer confused fixation probability with fixation rate
2026-04-30 · Day–Grok exchange: k = 800,000μ (N = 8e9, Nₑ = 1e4)
2026-01-05 · Independent Confirmation of Haldane's Limit: Haldane + d = 487
2026-01-05 · Day cites Kimura & Ohta 1969 for 'fixation time does not depend on recombination'
2026-01-08 · Day on Dawkins's Haldane figures: off by 87,916,307×
2026-01-10 · Day: Worden's O(1) bits/generation equals the Haldane-scale limit
2026-05-02 · Kimura's Fixation Calculator: Term 3 k_sel = s_max d / [2L ln(2Nₑ)] ≈ 8.3e-12
2026-05-07 · Retraction: Term 3 was misused as a bound on total k (adaptive only)
2026-05-07 · Same post: k = μ 'still falsified' — median factor 25 across 55 vertebrates
2026-05-07 · CHLCA revised to 250 kya–1.3 Mya (not 68–330 kya)
2026-05-23 · Probability Zero 2nd ed.: 14.9%, 410M base pairs (1st ed. used 40M bp from 2005)
2026-08-23 · Day on Chalub 2022: 1/(2N) is an assumption imported from Wright–Fisher
2026-08-26 · keruru: exact chains give P_fix = 1/(2N_census) to 15 decimals
2026-08-26 · keruru retracts his substitution-rate and aDNA claims (the day before Day's concession)
2026-08-26 · keruru: zero fixations in the aDNA window is the neutral prediction (~10^-29)
2026-08-27 · Hard Limits: census ceiling X = (Vₖ+2)G/16; the domain of k = μ is empty for large vertebrates
2026-08-27 · Hard Limits itself uses 1/(2N) as the start frequency (same day as the concession)
2026-08-27 · Day concedes: Kimura's identity never needed Nₑ; a 3rd edition is needed
2026-08-27 · Day: keruru's Nₑ ≈ 10⁴ presupposes k = μ; rs35619459 gives drift-variance Nₑ near 2
2026-01-10 · Holocene drift variance varied 3.3–4.6-fold (Day & Athos)
2026-08-31 · keruru: temporal-method Nₑ 8,139 / 9,835 with no μ, no coalescent
2026-09-14 · Hössjer (ally): rescaling MITTENS for μ and genome length leaves only ~2×
2026-09-14 · Hössjer: Haldane's cost of parallel selected fixations keeps the conclusion
2026-09-14 · Hössjer: neutral theory dates the divergence, so it cannot explain it
2026-09-17 · McCarthy: the human–chimp dates use Kimura's neutral result
2026-09-17 · McCarthy: mutations need not rise in frequency one at a time
2026-09-17 · McCarthy: 410M bp is structural variation; one event, many bp
2026-09-17 · McCarthy (time-adjusted): 400 billion × 1/20,000 = 20M
2026-09-17 · Day: the Darwillion is 'nothing more than a rhetorical absurdity'
2026-09-22 · Intrinsic Irrelevance: the pipeline is empty at generation zero; E[F] ≈ μL(T − 4Nₑ)
2026-09-22 · IR: ancestral polymorphism is 'a rounding error' (Nₑ = 10⁴: 1.44M)
2026-09-22 · IR: dating by k = μ is circular
2026-09-21 · Where the Errors Hide (Day–Athos, posted by Day): P(fix) = x₀ called wrong for real populations
2026-09-22 · Duffy (presenting Day): 252,000/1,400 = 180 fixations
2026-09-22 · Relayed population geneticist: 7.2M neutral differences, no selection
2026-09-22 · Day: 'confused mutations with fixations'
2026-09-28 · 3.0 explains the book's 1,400 (Good et al. summary) → own re-analysis 1,322
2026-09-28 · G_f = 1,322 (non-mutators, ≥95% snapshot rule)
2026-09-28 · Required fixations: 410M differences halved → 205M
2026-09-28 · 3.0 §7.3: 'a legitimate methodological concern' — SNV-only 17.5M, 91,600×
2026-09-28 · 3.0: supermutation does not scale linearly (100× → 8.5–17×)
2026-09-28 · 3.0 §8.1: the 45.4 fixations were fixed in parallel
2026-09-28 · 3.0: the 'post-Darwinian polythesis' fails comprehensively
2026-09-28 · r/DebateEvolution: 3.0's correction gives −906 'true fixations' in Ara−2
2026-09-28 · r/DebateEvolution: 3.0 §6.4 tenfold slip (3,840, not 38,400)
2026-09-28 · r/DebateEvolution: the LTEE is nonrecombining, one clone, one environment
2026-09-28 · r/DebateEvolution: bases affected by a rearrangement are not separate events
2026-09-28 · r/DebateEvolution: ~9.7M neutral substitutions over 252,000 generations (haploid)
2026-09-28 · Ghijselen: marathon analogy — runners run in parallel, so do fixations
2026-09-28 · Day to Dembski: 'The scaling element doesn’t apply at all'
2026-09-29 · aDNA v3 (Zenodo): 1 (v62) and 3 (v66) completions from >10%
2026-09-30 · Day: parallel fixation is 'clearly and specifically included' (reply to the marathon)
2026-09-27 · Blog-only NS rates: 4,615 per beneficial fixation; 'SERIAL' ~24,500
2026-10-01 · Mansfield: the pipeline would have been full at the split
2026-10-01 · Mansfield: the time BETWEEN fixations matters, not the time to fix one
2026-10-01 · Education post, first answer: the pipeline is 'functionally nonexistent'
2026-10-01 · Education post, UPDATE: 'The pipeline was full, but it was much shorter' (228,000 gens)
2026-10-01 · Day: MITTENS does not assume sequential fixation; 1,322 is total throughput
2026-01-19 · Q&A: t ≈ 19,800 generations per fixation (s = 0.001, Zeng 2021)
2026-10-01 · Education post: k = 32.3μ (Bergeron vs Yoo), no derivation
2026-10-01 · Day quotes Appendix A: 'Therefore fixation must be sequential' (180 vs 205M)
2026-10-01 · Day: 'perhaps I could have worded it better' (all-cause rate faster than sequential)
2026-10-01 · Snikker-Snak: Ara+2's 14 fixation events were all sequential
2026-10-01 · Day: either the specific fixations matter (Darwillion) or they are neutral noise
2026-10-02 · Myers: evolution is massively parallel
2026-10-02 · Fixation in the LTEE: strict 5,496 vs naive 8,679 ('including an earlier draft of our own')
2026-10-03 · Hancock: the formula assumes each mutation fixes before the next arises
2026-10-03 · Hancock: the 180 should be at least 360 (both lineages)
2026-10-03 · Hancock: ~76.8 neutral fixations per generation (diploid basis)
2026-10-03 · Hancock corrects on screen: use the haploid 3.2e9, not 6.4e9; keeps 76 via SV-inclusive count
2026-10-03 · Hancock: ~38M neutral differences over two lineages
2026-10-03 · Hancock: 205M needs ~407 per generation
2026-10-03 · Hancock: neutral supply alone predicts ~22,000 gens/fixation in E. coli (μ ≈ 1e-11)
2026-10-04 · KITTENS: 1.1M shortfall = 94,000 (supply) × 11.7 (bp vs events)
2026-10-04 · KITTENS concedes: an illustration, not a proof of linear scaling
2026-10-04 · KITTENS §11: 3.0's §8.2 and Appendix D revert to the interval form
2026-10-04 · Myers after Day's reply: 'he thinks evolution is a simple serial process'
2026-10-05 · Nesslig20: μ_G = 75 → ~37.8M neutral fixed differences
2026-10-05 · Nesslig20: Haldane's cost limit does not apply to drift
2026-10-05 · Best They've Got I: 'No one calculated a smaller space' (Wistar)
2026-10-06 · Relictation: p = 1/(2N) 'holds exactly regardless of offspring distribution'
2026-10-07 · Audit B3: P_fix = 1/(2N) for every Nₑ; Nₑ sets the timescale
2026-10-07 · Audit B1: Day's formula exact for an empty start; equilibrium start gives U·T
2026-10-07 · Audit F1: without interference many fixations are in flight at once
2026-10-07 · Audit R2 note: Term 3 allows ~7.7× more than Haldane + d
2026-10-08 · Audit R4: same-basis ratio is 17.1 (7.7 mixed bases, withdrawn)
2026-10-08 · Audit H2-hard first draft: 'literal 1/300 falsified'
2026-10-08 · Audit H2-hard (reviewed): 10% is not a general bound; cap is ln R / D; Haldane's regime untested
2026-10-08 · Audit H: soft selection did not remove the cost (against the critics' stock reply)
2026-10-08 · Audit H (pre-review): 'soft within 15% of hard' — withdrawn
2026-10-08 · Audit B1c: empty-start premise contradicted (and withdrawn by Day)
2026-10-08 · Audit B4a: d − 2μT = θ_anc; at Nₑ,anc = 1e4 d is half the observed (Day-side point)
2026-10-08 · Audit B4a draft: CSAC 14–22% 'tension' (compared with θ_anc/d) — deleted
2026-10-08 · Audit B4a: Hancock 38M / Nesslig20 37.8M double-count on an SNV basis
2026-10-08 · Audit B3b/B3c: B&L effect real; RRME 0.743 a window artefact
2026-10-08 · Audit C1: the aDNA test does not discriminate
2026-10-08 · Audit C6: 'this does not rescue Day' withdrawn as unsupported
2026-10-08 · Audit C1b: the 21-count is not reproducible from the published procedure
2026-10-08 · Audit A-sim: G_f ≈ 1,300 reproducible; asexual response sublinear; recombination factor extrapolated
2026-10-08 · Audit F2: free recombination R_int 0.975 at 272 loci (first draft said 'contradicted at r = 1/2')
2026-08-26 · keruru: fossil-calibrated rate ~2× the pedigree rate (unreconciled)
2026-09-14 · Hössjer: MITTENS with 2019 inputs and d gives 127; ×125 for μ gives 15,800
2024-07-13 · Day on Wright's twenty questions: dice have no cumulative result
2022-05-18 · Rosenhouse 2022 ch.4 (via Felsenstein): the Wistar critiques were refuted
2022-08-26 · Dembski (ally) on Rosenhouse: 'objectively bad'; the Weasel's fitness function supplies the information
2026-01-29 · Camestros: a serious treatment would discuss developments since 1966
2026-09-28 · Probability Zero 2nd ed. ch.6 (posted on Dembski's Substack): 'The biologists did not answer the mathematicians'
2026-10-05 · Best They've Got I: Ulam 'will come to Eden's conclusions'
2026-10-07 · Audit fidelity: the sentence attributed to Ulam is not in the volume's OCR text
2026-10-06 · Best They've Got II: Rosenhouse ch.4 has no quantitative refutation
2026-09-12 · Probability Weasel: 540,000 generations; the Weasel 'demonstrates the precise opposite'
